defs_parts: Eight labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
In the glossary: the term is on the course term list, but the text does not explain it.
Editor or docs: the term comes from the editor itself or its official documentation.
Video only: the term comes from a video lecture, and is not in the course text or on the term list.
Outside source: the term comes from a source outside the course text.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Simulation: a model run step by step from stated rules, not a measurement of a real game.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: A keyframe is a stored value, and interpolation computes the in-betweens.
Easing is the speed curve. Ease-in starts slow, and ease-out ends slow.
Timing is how long a move takes, and spacing is where its frames fall.
Anticipation is the wind-up, and squash and stretch shows speed and impact.
FK takes angles and gives the hand, and IK takes a target and gives angles.
A blend tree mixes clips by weight, and a state machine picks one clip.
bookends.command: Give me short cases from making a game, one at a time, each showing an animation problem or choice. Draw on keyframe, tween, ease-in, ease-out, timing, spacing, loop seam, anticipation, IK and root motion. I answer with the exact term and say why its look-alike does not fit. Wait for my answer before you reveal yours, then say whether I was right.
checks: Check: each case is about making a game, and the answer waits for you.
Check: you named the exact term and ruled out its look-alike.
